fact_text: NCCPL publishes daily FIPI and LIPI reports that break gross and net buying and selling into foreign investors, overseas Pakistanis, local companies and local individuals, which shows who is trading each day.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Stock Market Manipulation Myth BUSTED! Can Big Players Manipulate Stocks?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Free float is the share of a listed company's shares that are actually available for public trading; the rest is held by the company's own holders. The video uses 20% free float as its example.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Stock Market Manipulation Myth BUSTED! Can Big Players Manipulate Stocks?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Market capitalisation is total shares multiplied by share price, while free-float market cap multiplies only the tradable float by price, giving the value of shares open to the public.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Stock Market Manipulation Myth BUSTED! Can Big Players Manipulate Stocks?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Free float of well-established PSX companies is generally below 50% of shares, so the tradable stock is usually a minority of the company and a single holder cannot readily sell all of it.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Stock Market Manipulation Myth BUSTED! Can Big Players Manipulate Stocks?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The PSX circuit breaker halts trading in a stock once its price moves 10% in a session, capping how far one day's price can be pushed and giving holders time to cancel open orders.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Stock Market Manipulation Myth BUSTED! Can Big Players Manipulate Stocks?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Stocks priced at Rs 10 or below have a tighter session move limit of Rs 1, so small-priced shares can show large percentage moves even though the circuit breaker still applies.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Stock Market Manipulation Myth BUSTED! Can Big Players Manipulate Stocks?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pushing a large company's price down needs buyers on the other side; a large holder dumping shares without demand does not move the price much, which is a practical test of claimed single-player control.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Stock Market Manipulation Myth BUSTED! Can Big Players Manipulate Stocks?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Claims that big players control the PSX ignore dispersed holdings across banks, insurers, mutual funds and retail investors, which makes coordinated control of large companies unlikely in the analyst's view.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Stock Market Manipulation Myth BUSTED! Can Big Players Manipulate Stocks?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst notes that early holders of a stock who have already profited sometimes promote it through tip or signal groups, and later buyers who follow the signals can end up holding shares sold to them by those early holders.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Stock Market Manipulation Myth BUSTED! Can Big Players Manipulate Stocks?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A viral claim that three asset managers hold 88% of S&P 500 companies was checked against data and found to be far off, showing that concentration claims should be verified before they are repeated.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Stock Market Manipulation Myth BUSTED! Can Big Players Manipulate Stocks?' (YouTube transcript, undated)
